Class YahooSymbolSearch

java.lang.Object
grafioschtrader.connector.securitysearch.BaseSecuritySearchProvider
grafioschtrader.connector.yahoo.YahooSymbolSearch
All Implemented Interfaces:
ISecuritySearchProvider
@Component public class YahooSymbolSearch extends BaseSecuritySearchProvider
Searches Yahoo Finance listings through its public symbol search. At Yahoo, the symbol of a non-US share usually carries an exchange suffix: NOVN.SW is Novartis on the SIX Swiss Exchange.

Yahoo returns neither ISIN nor currency, so both stay IdentityEvidence.UNKNOWN; a search by ISIN is a full-text search, not a filter. The MIC is derived from mic_provider_map, which holds one Yahoo exchange code and symbol suffix per MIC. Yahoo does not always answer with that code - Novartis comes back as EBS instead of SWX - so a candidate is placed on a MIC when

  1. its exchange code or its symbol suffix equals the mapping of the queried MIC, or else
  2. its exchange code maps to exactly one MIC, or else
  3. its symbol suffix maps to exactly one MIC.
A segment MIC found this way is folded into its operating MIC (NMS → XNMS → XNAS). Otherwise the MIC stays unknown. A missing mapping of the queried MIC is no error; it only leaves the MIC unknown.

When the ISIN search yields no candidate on the queried exchange, the ticker is searched as well, because Yahoo often knows an ISIN only for one of several listings. All Yahoo searches of the application share the request budget of this bean (two tokens, one more every two seconds), as Yahoo answers bursts with HTTP 429.

Master data comes from the meta block of the chart endpoint the Yahoo price connector also uses: currency, name, instrument type and firstTradeDate. The currency is the identity check of a Yahoo listing, because the search delivers none. The first trade date of the listing becomes the first active day, but not before the oldest trading day GT keeps prices for (GlobalConstants.OLDEST_TRADING_DAY). Yahoo is no exchange, so it sets neither a product nor an exchange hyperlink.
